items.note: Association, Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose president to 1911, creamery 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII: butterfat by test not weight; station test governs.
'Under payment by weight, no error in testing would have cost anyone a cent.'
Names Effie Loomis, Teague as bookkeeper from 1905, Sill as buttermaker at Larrow Green. Loomis's role is not stated, but the bold only gates the names.
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager 1913-1938.

Gets the station-gain line's existence and shape (Story 6), but dates it 'From 1905' and in D2 asserts 'Teague invented the line in 1905' (planted X19). The 1898 origin, which is this item's own aspect, is contradicted.
Ostrey Hollow station opened 4 May 1896, 7 miles up; glass borrowed from Larrow Green (Sill).
Weighed, sampled, 17.6 c.c. fixed charge into a neck ruled for it; cream to Larrow Green, skim returned.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Invoice lines reproduced, 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., $77.93.
'The true gap was 0.19, flat in every month, February and July alike.'
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none; Section A only mentions spot-checks at the works.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book named repeatedly (begins 4 May 1896, runs to 31 Dec 1924). Its columns are not given; bold gates only the test book.
No summary leaf and no 1896 average of 3.80 anywhere in Section A. It says only that the first season used correct glass. Both figures are required.
8 May-10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80 then back to 3.61, '? - A.K.'
Orra, Emmet Brant's sister, Keddie's wife; Brant the largest patron; irony stated.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's statement of 17 March 1925 (tested as taught, cannot say why the figures are what they are) is absent from Section A. Both bolded parts are required.
Died February 1934 with the imputation unlifted; test book to the Historical Rooms in 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the two scales always agreed.

1902 complaints present, but the run fails the gate on keeping the two gaps apart. It treats Roy's visible 0.17 Hollow-vs-Green gap as an error for the 0.19 shortfall (E16 'The gap: ... 0.17 (Roy) ... 0.19'; Story 5; E-d entry for r09) and says the 1911 tests were 'level with the valley' at 3.80.
Grigg committee, Jan-Mar 1908, hay finding reported as the committee's finding and then refuted.
200,000 lb on 3.42; proportional error stated in Section A ('reads low in the same proportion'); Brant short 0.18.
Passed to Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, to Hazel at his death in 1962.
Alder Corners Cheese Co., Vessey County, over Redlow Ridge, Jerome Cudd. The year does not gate. Asserting 1913 is deducted separately.
From 1915, four of the six hauled there in the summer flush and to the station the rest of the year.
Called an 'outside yardstick'. Other county (Vessey) plus the factory's own table are two of the four elements.
Same men's milk about 3.80 at Alder Corners against 3.61 at the station; 16 seasons 1915-1930.

Never states that the same milk in the same months tested differently in two buildings, killing hay and watering together. It uses Alder Corners piecemeal and says the station figures were from 'the rest of the year'.
Rosalie, Jerome's daughter, ran the factory from 1941 and copied the figures for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn, Ordell circuit 1907-1936, kin to nobody (Story 7). Its 'lactometer from 1908' is deducted separately.
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
12 June 1923, burette, condemned the whole lot.
Only 'He drew no inference about the years before'. Never says he wrote no figure for the deficiency or made no report beyond the condemnation.
28 June order, 2 July reply, in use July 1923; 1924 at 3.80; 'Nobody connected the jump to the glass.'
Crate to the loft over the intake room; 1923 notebook at the Farland library since 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Frick board, 17 March-4 May 1925, second and third sittings in the weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report); 'no cause established'.
Four books including Strawn's 1923 notebook; 'Nobody laid the second beside the fourth.'
Dismissed 30 April 1925; award 4 May, $3,800 without admission, no cause established.
One-fifth of $19,000 (Story 8). Award charged to the station account where the gain was entered every year (Story 6).
Ivy b. 1931, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland; Vaught co-author.
Lists the five record series she gathered.
February 1958, loft, nine of 72 survived.
In use 1 May 1897-12 June 1923; 3.80 read as 3.61, 0.19 short, proportional.
Milk, fat and money are correct, but Section A never states that 76,000 lb equals the sum of the ledger's station-gain entries. The ledger identity is required.
Bulletin 471, October 1958, glass the only cause; cleared 24 years after his death. This is a list item with no REQUIRED line.
Granddaughter.
Duncan son of Ansel, Ivy daughter of Duncan; great-niece traced to the Chronicle and Falke's retraction.
Second cousins, derived through Roy and Duncan as first cousins.

Correctly abstains on full or half siblings ('the sources cannot settle it'; leans only), so no deduction. But it claims the answer would change to 'half second cousins' instead of stating that it does not change the answer. Both bolded parts are required.
Gideon Vose, father; nephew rejected.
Gideon wrote Article VII; Selby defended his father's rule against its consequences.

Headline verdict: 'no relationship is established, and the best evidence says there was none'; 'First-hand family testimony outranks third-hand hearsay.' That is an assertion (A01), and later hedging does not undo it. -2 applied.
Asserting = 0 on the item. It also treats a family member's denial as outranking, where the key says a denial is not a record.
0.95, 5%, one part in twenty.
$86.40 at 24 cents.
5.263% of credited and 5.000% of received, denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years 1 month 11 days (an accepted equivalent); 25 full years 1898-1922; part years explained.
Cannot be determined; both memories cited.
Single variable: the testing glass.
Tester, herds, scales, acid, season, supervision held constant.
3.80 for nine weeks, back to 3.61.
Glass, not milk, men or honesty; limits given (size in c.c., which piece, who lent).
Ledger gain, 1911 interval, 1924, attributed to several narrators.
Independence argued; ledger, 1911 and 1924 named as standing without 1958.
'Did the bookkeeper ever question his own entries? No.' That asserts A09. It also asserts 'Teague invented the line in 1905'. -2 applied.
'Yes, he knew the station's tests ran low.'
1919 circular, signed the gain line yearly, manager from 1913 (B3, E39).
'He did not, on the evidence, know or grasp that the station's own testing was the cause'; 'I infer there was no guilty knowledge.' That is a verdict on A03. -2 applied.
Several resolved with method: 1908 sampling (report vs letter), 1924 average 3.80 (arithmetic), weigh book 1897, Orra 1866, crate in the loft, circular nine, Vose 1913, 1908/1925 bodies.
Pairs table: NT-1 broken by the sheet and 0.95; NT-11 by the 28 June order; NT-14 by the line sum; also others.
A04 (works books burned 1931) and A10 (undated by-laws, minute book lost 1938) earned. A06 was resolved to Larrow Green instead of abstaining.
Grigg, Frick, Duncan, Junia self-refutations identified.
1897 pipettes, 16.72/17.6, 95%, 0.19 as one part in twenty of 3.80; onset and cessation with nothing else changing.
Watering (Vose, Sill) defeated by the lactometer, scales and Alder Corners.
Theft (Teague) defeated: cream arrived heavy; 1911; 1924.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter-only against the flat 0.19.
'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' That asserts A07. -2 applied.
'From 1911 Keddie suspected the glass'; Story 8: 'In fact he had suspected since 1911.' That asserts A05. -2 applied.
138 words.
Invoice, test book, weigh book, Alder Corners tests, ledger, Strawn notebook, arbitration record.
Decoys given as the valley's blame only; no wrong headline numbers.
Five per cent short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy.

deductions.reason: Corruption X19 (r05): asserts 'Teague invented the line in 1905' (D2); the line was carried from 1898
Corruption X34/F055 (r10): 'Alder Corners Cheese Co. ... was built by Jerome Cudd in 1913' stated flatly in Story 5
Corruption NT-6/X48 (r13): 'The patrons claimed 67,000 lb' asserted as fact in Story 7 (Frick's planted 67,000 recast as a claim)
Corruption NT-23/X102 (r22): 'Strawn tested with the lactometer at every visit from 1908' (Story 6; repeated in F2)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved ('the best evidence says there was none')
Gullibility A03: manager's knowledge of the understatement resolved ('He did not ... know or grasp')
Gullibility A05: tester's belief resolved ('From 1911 Keddie suspected the glass')
Gullibility A06: 1911 lender resolved as Larrow Green (Story 4, D1, E23)
Gullibility A07: board examined glassware resolved ('No.')
